Placement of the Knots of the Spline Models

Source: R/spline_knot_table.R
spline_knot_table.Rd

Reports the internal knots of the Royston-Parmar spline models of each fit (each arm of the independent fits and both arms together for the dependent fit) with the Kaplan-Meier estimate at each knot, as in the table of knot placement of a survival analysis report.

Usage

spline_knot_table(x)

Arguments

x

Object returned by fit_survival_models.

Value

A data frame with the columns fit_type, arm, n_knots, knot (index of the knot), quantile (probability of the quantile of the log event times; for knots given by the user, the proportion of log event times at or below the knot), log_time, time, n_risk, surv_est and surv_se. It has no rows when no spline model was fitted.

Details

The knots are the same for the hazard, odds and normal scales. The number at risk and the Kaplan-Meier estimate are those of the data fitted (both arms pooled for the dependent fit) at the knot time; a knot at an observed time counts the patients with that time as at risk and their events in the estimate. The standard error is that of Greenwood.

Examples

dat <- processing_dataset(
  system.file("extdata", "fit_example.csv", package = "SurvFitSummary"),
  column_arm = "TRT01P", column_survtime = "AVAL", column_cnsr = "CNSR",
  control_arm = "Control"
)
fits <- fit_survival_models(dat, distributions = NULL,
                            spline_scales = "hazard")
spline_knot_table(fits)
